prompt: Reach past the private keyword: read and overwrite a private field by name using reflection. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: getDeclaredField finds a field at any access level on the class itself, and setAccessible(true) switches off the access check that would otherwise make get and set throw IllegalAccessException. Field.get returns Object, so primitives arrive boxed -- an int field hands you an Integer -- and Field.set accepts the boxed form and unboxes it on the way in. This power is exactly why reflection is reserved for tools such as test frameworks, serializers and injection containers: ordinary code should go through the class's own API and respect the private keyword.
hints: Both methods start the same way: target.getClass().getDeclaredField(name), then setAccessible(true).
Field.get takes the object to read FROM, so it is field.get(target), not field.get().
The methods declare throws Exception, so you do not need a try/catch -- just let NoSuchFieldException and IllegalAccessException propagate to the caller.
